stories.headline: Heat deaths doubled in Belgium during the June 2026 heat wave
stories.what_happened: A new rapid attribution study by Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) finds that human-induced climate change made the June 2026 heat wave in Belgium 3.9°C hotter and more than doubled the number of heat-related deaths. Of the estimated 1,181 deaths statistically linked to the extreme temperatures recorded between June 17 and 28, 2026, 665—or 56%—would not have occurred without anthropogenic climate change. This is the first time heat-related deaths during a specific Belgian heat wave have been attributed to human-induced climate change.

stories.headline: Interactive 3D technology reveals hidden tumors during surgery

The new technology uses augmented reality to overlay a 3D visualization of the tumor and other anatomical structures on the surgeon's camera view. The visualization is updated as the camera changes position.

stories.headline: Research shows risk-taking behavior precedes increased alcohol consumption, not vice versa
stories.what_happened: A study has found that increases in risk-taking behavior in people with mild to moderate alcohol use disorder (AUD) precede increases in alcohol consumption, not vice versa. This research is the first to predict changes in real-life drinking longitudinally using gamified smartphone-based decision-making tasks. The findings from the study, appearing in Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, open up the possibility of future targeted and timely interventions for people with AUD.
